outcome.answer: The closest matches are sparse-retrieval papers that use dense models or dense embeddings as a starting point, but none directly answer a generic “dense to sparse retrieval” request in full. [1] presents learned sparse retrievers that bridge the gap with dense models while using less index memory, [2] shows dense retrievers can be decomposed into sparse BM25-ready features, and [7] uses sparse autoencoders to train sparse retrieval models from LLM representations. [10] is also relevant because it replaces multi-vector dense-style retrieval bottlenecks with sparse coding and inverted indexing.
